html:
The Jicarilla are an eastern Apache people of northern New Mexico and southern Colorado. Their name is Mexican Spanish for "little basket", after the small sealed baskets they used as drinking cups.

They lived a half-settled life in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and the plains to the east, moving between hunting grounds, gathering places and small farms along the rivers. They learned farming and pottery from the Pueblo peoples, and ranged onto the Great Plains from before 1525.

In the 1700s the Comanche drove them off the plains, and they turned to Spanish New Mexico for protection. They allied often with the Ute. After decades of moves the United States gave them a reservation in northern New Mexico in 1887, the home of the Jicarilla Apache Nation today. The map also shows them as Jicarilla Apache.
sum: The Jicarilla are an eastern Apache people of northern New Mexico and southern Colorado. Their name is Mexican Spanish for "little basket", after the small sealed baskets they used as drinking cups.
